# LCM Nav3D

> An industry-leading, production-grade, heavily optimised sparse voxel octree navigation plugin for Unreal Engine, built for AAA-scale projects. It pathfinds through true 3D volume rather than a walkable surface, for flying, swimming and free-floating agents and Mass Entity crowds. GPU voxelization and GPU 6-DOF compute with automatic CPU fallback, asynchronous pathfinding, deterministic results, explicit frame-budget controls and World Partition support. Complete C++ source, Blueprint exposed.

LCM Nav3D is an industry-leading, production-grade, heavily optimised navigation
plugin for Unreal Engine 5.2 to 5.8 (Windows 64-bit and Linux), built for AAA-scale
projects. It ships complete C++ source and is fully exposed to Blueprint.

Engineering characteristics: GPU voxelization and GPU 6-DOF compute with automatic
CPU fallback when no GPU is present; asynchronous pathfinding off the game thread;
deterministic results, so replays, lockstep multiplayer and automated tests are
reproducible; explicit frame-budget controls, with dynamic-obstacle updates
coalesced into a single window rather than restamped per event; a sparse octree
whose memory cost is driven by how cluttered a level is rather than how large it
is; World Partition and streaming support with a bake path; and 10,000+ agent
crowds through the Mass Entity ECS with LOD-culled rendering.

Unreal's stock Recast navmesh represents a walkable *surface* and answers
"where can I stand?". LCM Nav3D represents the navigable *volume* and answers
"where is there empty air?", which is what flying, swimming and free-floating
agents need. The two run side by side in the same level.

Key terms: volumetric 3D navigation, sparse voxel octree (SVO) pathfinding, flying
AI, Unreal Engine, drone and dragon navigation, underwater navigation, Mass Entity
crowds, true-3D Environment Query System (EQS), Behavior Tree, StateTree.

This file follows the llms.txt convention. Every page below is plain HTML with no
client-side rendering, so the URLs can be fetched directly.

## Start here

- [Overview](https://lcmnav3d.github.io/): Production-grade volumetric 3D navigation for Unreal Engine 5. GPU-accelerated sparse voxel octree pathfinding, 10,000+ Mass Entity agents and true-3D EQS.
- [Nav3D vs Recast](https://lcmnav3d.github.io/nav3d-vs-recast.html): Why Unreal's Recast navmesh cannot represent open air, where each flying-AI workaround breaks down, and when volumetric SVO navigation is the right answer instead.

## Getting started

- [Installation](https://lcmnav3d.github.io/installation.html): Step-by-step install of the LCM Nav3D plugin into an Unreal Engine 5.2-5.8 project, from Fab or by hand, plus how to verify the install with a demo map.
- [Core concepts](https://lcmnav3d.github.io/core-concepts.html): How LCM Nav3D carves empty air into a sparse voxel octree and paths through it. Covers the navigation manager actor, world extent, voxel size and clearance.
- [Your first flying agent](https://lcmnav3d.github.io/your-first-flying-agent.html): Build a pawn that flies through true 3D space to a goal in Unreal Engine, using a navigation manager, an AIController and one LCM Fly To task. No C++ needed.
- [The same agent in StateTree](https://lcmnav3d.github.io/statetree-agent.html): Author identical 3D flight behaviour in StateTree instead of a Behavior Tree. Swap RunBehaviorTree for a StateTreeAIComponent and bind the Fly To task target.
- [Dynamic obstacles](https://lcmnav3d.github.io/dynamic-obstacles.html): Add a Dynamic Obstacle component to any moving actor. LCM Nav3D restamps the octree and agents reroute live around doors, platforms and destructible cover.

## Going further

- [Mass Entity crowds](https://lcmnav3d.github.io/mass-entity-crowds.html): Add one trait to a Mass Entity Config and a crowd navigates in full 3D through the Unreal ECS. No per-agent controller, no tick function and no code required.
- [Tactical EQS in true 3D](https://lcmnav3d.github.io/tactical-eqs.html): LCM Nav3D ships EQS generators and tests that work in true 3D: candidate points anywhere in the navigable volume, scored by volumetric line-of-sight and cover.
- [AI perception](https://lcmnav3d.github.io/ai-perception.html): Wire Unreal's UAIPerceptionComponent into LCM Nav3D through the AI Perception Bridge, so perceived threats feed true-3D EQS queries for flanking and cover.
- [Hybrid Recast + Nav3D](https://lcmnav3d.github.io/hybrid-recast.html): Run walking agents on Recast and flying agents on the SVO in one level. The Crowd Avoidance Bridge lets Detour RVO steer Recast agents around LCM Nav3D pawns.
- [Nav links and area modifiers](https://lcmnav3d.github.io/nav-links-and-areas.html): Vertical ladders, jump shafts and teleporters via ULcmNavLinkComponent, plus volumetric cost overlays for water, storms and danger zones via NavArea modifiers.
- [The Gameplay Debugger](https://lcmnav3d.github.io/gameplay-debugger.html): LCM Nav3D adds its own category to Unreal's stock Gameplay Debugger. Press the debugger key in PIE, pick an agent and read per-agent and plugin-wide state live.

## Behaviour Tree patterns

- [Wait](https://lcmnav3d.github.io/bt-wait.html): Unreal Engine's stock Wait task works as-is with LCM Nav3D flying agents. The pattern, why no plugin variant ships, and the one LCM Nav3D-specific alternative.
- [Is At Location](https://lcmnav3d.github.io/bt-is-at-location.html): UBTDecorator_IsAtLocation already works on LCM Nav3D pawns. Three-step usage, why no plugin-specific variant exists, and when the path-finding variant helps.
- [Look At](https://lcmnav3d.github.io/bt-look-at.html): Unreal's stock Rotate to Face BB Entry task covers both LookAt and TurnInPlace for LCM Nav3D agents. Setup, tuning and when a custom rotation task is worth it.
- [Turn In Place](https://lcmnav3d.github.io/bt-turn-in-place.html): Turn an LCM Nav3D agent in place with Unreal's stock rotation task, and hold facing during other tasks with the DefaultFocus service. Plus constant-rate turns.
- [Health Below](https://lcmnav3d.github.io/bt-health-below.html): Unreal ships all you need: a Float blackboard key plus a Blackboard-Compare decorator. The pattern, a GameplayTag variant, and why no LCM Nav3D node ships.
- [Perception Relay](https://lcmnav3d.github.io/bt-perception-relay.html): UAIPerceptionComponent already emits perception updates as a delegate. Bind it in your AI controller and write to a blackboard key - no custom BT service needed.
- [Memory Decay](https://lcmnav3d.github.io/bt-memory-decay.html): Unreal's UAIPerceptionComponent already tracks per-actor last-known stimulus location with age. Use it as a BT service instead of a hand-rolled decay timer.

## Reference

- [Editor tools](https://lcmnav3d.github.io/editor-tools.html): Every LCM Nav3D panel behind the Nav3D toolbar button: the Welcome screen, Manager panel, Bake Volumes, Setup Wizard, Health Check and the Auto-Tuner.
- [Settings reference](https://lcmnav3d.github.io/settings.html): Every field on the LCM Nav3D navigation manager, with verified defaults and limits: setup, voxels, collision, performance, skeleton, debug and runtime state.
- [Troubleshooting](https://lcmnav3d.github.io/troubleshooting.html): LCM Nav3D problems in the order people hit them: agents that will not move, "no path found", ignored geometry, dead dynamic obstacles and performance issues.
- [Flight and locomotion](https://lcmnav3d.github.io/flight-locomotion.html): Physically plausible 6-DOF locomotion for drones, birds and fish, layered on LCM Nav3D guidance. Archetypes, the animation contract, tuning and determinism.
- [Mass traits reference](https://lcmnav3d.github.io/mass-traits.html): Every LCM Nav3D Mass Entity trait, the combination matrix, the editor validator and the one rule you must not break: exactly one movement trait per agent.
- [API reference](https://lcmnav3d.github.io/api-reference.html): Every LCM Nav3D class, function and property you can reach from Blueprint, the Details panel, a Behaviour Tree, a StateTree or a Mass Entity config.
